head: 408ae68f9e445fc911f713d5bbb3a64dda1ab9fe
line: 408ae68f9e445fc911f713d5bbb3a64dda1ab9fe:corpus/knowledge/line-binding-r31.md:22:RFC 5147 [S057] names parts of a text/plain entity by line position or line range, and it counts differently: "Line position counting starts with zero, so the line position before the first line of a text/plain MIME entity has the line position zero" (§2.2.3). A position sits *between* lines; a range runs from one position to another (§2.2.4). The gate's `at=` and the C1 `"line"` field number the lines themselves from 1. So RFC `line=3,5` (positions 3 to 5) covers the gate's lines 4 and 5, which is `"line":"4-5"`. Never copy an RFC fragment index into `"line"` without converting it.

head: 0b518f568da7b40a4ab026508d63c942faa7badf
line: 0b518f568da7b40a4ab026508d63c942faa7badf:corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r4-14-libsignal.md:41:- claim: `rea-agents@6.4.0 analyze <libsignal.node>` on the 24.9 MB stripped binary **fails RC=1** after ~330 s with typed JSON `{code:"provider_timeout", details:{operation:"list_documents", timeout_ms:330000}}` — Ghidra's headless import+auto-analysis exceeds the bridge's readiness deadline; the analysis itself was still mid-flight (decompiler stage) when the bridge gave up. The deadline is a config knob, not a law: `dist/config/ghidraStartupTimeout.js` declares `DEFAULT_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS = 330_000` bound to env `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` (positive int, up to i32 max) via `dist/config/environment.js`. Re-running with `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS=1140000` lets the same binary proceed past 330 s. Operational corollaries: REA's `analyze`/`search`/`decompile` all accept `--snapshot <file>` ("load and update a local analysis snapshot") — mandatory on big targets so one Ghidra pass amortizes across verbs; and killing the wrapping shell does NOT kill the `npx`/`node`/`java` tree (run 1 survived `kill_shell`, had to be killed by PID).

line: 0b518f568da7b40a4ab026508d63c942faa7badf:corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r4-14-libsignal.md:87:signal-desktop's two big `.node` addons are neon-1.1.1 Rust modules of the r3 family-B species — zero ` U napi` imports, N-API bound lazily by `dlopen/dlsym` into `.data.rel.ro` thunks, both exporting the same sub-600-byte TLS-gated trampoline `napi_register_module_v1` that walks `linkme`/`linkm2` distributed slices. The headline recovery result: **stripping does not hide the JS surface** — libsignal's entire export table survives as 741 `D`-type `signal_register_node_*` descriptors `{name_ptr,name_len,shim_fn_ptr}` (560 production + 181 `TESTING_*` names resolved byte-exact via reloc addends), while ringrtc's ~40 `ringrtc::electron::*` export names persist in panic strings, so both APIs enumerate with `nm -D`/`strings` alone, no decompiler needed. Panic-location `.rs` paths double as a versioned SBOM (163 crates incl. neon-1.1.1/tokio-1.52.3/curve25519-dalek-5.0.0) and module map (`libsignal_net`, `libsignal_protocol`, `zkgroup`, `spqr` post-quantum ratchet); `.comment` pins rustc 1.99-nightly vs 1.97.1 and `.gnu_debuglink` names the shipped `.debug` companion. REA side: ringrtc `analyze` landed clean — `ev_9e89880c…`, ghidra 12.1.4, 36 segments / 28,122 procedures / 12,276 strings in 304 s. libsignal `analyze` hit the wall twice, measured honestly: stock 330 s `provider_timeout` at `list_documents`, then a proven-honored `REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS=1140000` retry still timed out at 1,142 s mid-decompile under r4 fleet CPU contention (load ~16, sibling AnalyzeHeadless jobs on 91/41 MB targets). Two operational corrections recorded for later lanes: `--snapshot` stores a binding manifest, not a program cache — every CLI verb re-pays the full Ghidra import+analysis (a `search` on ringrtc spawned a fresh project and exceeded 300 s); and `kill_shell` does not reap the `npx→node→java` tree — orphan Ghidra jobs keep burning cores after their wrapper dies.

head: 0b518f568da7b40a4ab026508d63c942faa7badf
line: 0b518f568da7b40a4ab026508d63c942faa7badf:corpus/knowledge/2026-10-13-r3-node-addons.md:36:- claim: Full `.node` census under `*.asar.unpacked` = 7 modules across 3 apps. Family A — classic dynamic N-API (undefined `napi_*` resolved from the host's exports): obsidian `btime` (36), `get-fonts` (39), signal `fs-xattr` (21), signal `@signalapp+sqlcipher` (51). Family B — zero undefined `napi_*`, imports `dlopen`/`dlsym` instead and resolves the API lazily at init: `@signalapp+libsignal-client.node` (24.9 MB, stripped), `libringrtc-x64.node` (14.5 MB, stripped, +libpulse), `/opt/1Password/resources/app.asar.unpacked/index.node` (**187,997,016 B**, not stripped, sha256 `1cb3e361ae85c304544d7b9b063e5eacec4f20c7009ce504e8f93f4d48fa7778`). All family-B modules still export `napi_register_module_v1` — but they don't need a matching host `.dynsym` for every `napi_*` call, which is why Rust napi-rs/Neon builds survive host API drift. Tell-tales: 1Password's `.comment` shows `Linker: LLD 22.1.8` + `rustc version 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01)` + Ubuntu GCC 9.4.0/clang 15.0.7 (mixed Rust/C build); it exports `rust_u2f_*` C-ABI fns and `__start/stop_linkm{e,2}_{EXPORTS,MAIN}` section-boundary symbols (Rust `linkme` distributed-slice registration). libsignal exports `signal_register_node_*` as **`D` data** symbols — registration descriptors a top-level register function walks, not callable exports.

line: 7765969c79e6f3df44cce2e303e6a0cf2b054d8b:tools/fixtures/mori-oom-killers/cases-a2.json:9:   "why": "Core A2-01 firing: an in-scope suppressed line makes the scope incomplete and, with no positive evidence, an active earlyoom then reads KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2. Rule A2-01 (round-27/contract.md:49) says a journald `Suppressed N messages from earlyoom.service` line in scope sets scope_complete false; the rule was adopted as A1b in round-26/contract.md:158-159. Journal record 1 is the invocation's version line `earlyoom 1.9.0` at 42000000, exactly ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic=42000000, so it is inside the scope (round-26/contract.md:78-79: scope is the current invocation's lines in the current boot whose __MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP is >= ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic; the version line is main.c:161 `fprintf(stderr, \"earlyoom \" VERSION \"\\n\")` at earlyoom v1.9.0). Journal record 2, `Suppressed 42 messages from earlyoom.service` at 42001234, is also inside the scope, so scope_complete is false (round-26/contract.md:92-93 defines scope_complete as true only when the version line of the current invocation is inside the scope; A2-01 adds the in-scope suppressed line as a second disqualifier). No `sending SIG... to process` line and no escalation line is in scope and oomd_notices is 0, so there is no positive evidence (round-26/contract.md:97-98); an active earlyoom with scope_complete false is KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 (round-26/contract.md:99-101). earlyoom.state is active because the show text carries ActiveState=active (round-26/contract.md:91; the same mapping frozen in cases.json c01/c04/c13). earlyoom.version is 1.9.0 because the version line is in scope (round-26/contract.md:82 with :78-79). earlyoom.dryrun is false because no `dryrun mode enabled` line is in scope and the output spec gives dryrun no null alternative (round-26/contract.md:89 and :94; frozen cases.json c01/c19). oomd.state inactive and oomd.notices_this_boot 0 follow the oomd show text and the oomd_notices input (round-26/contract.md:95; frozen cases.json c01/c06). Deliberately not pinned: earlyoom.grammar, because round-26/contract.md:91 lists the two grammar values but states no condition for choosing between them, and the two readings that fit the frozen set (verified when the in-scope version line reads 1.9.0, versus verified only for a complete scope) disagree exactly for this input; earlyoom.actions, because frozen case c05 declines to pin the counts of an active reader whose scope is incomplete; earlyoom.thresholds, because round-26/contract.md:92 gives thresholds a null alternative and frozen case c04, also an incomplete scope, leaves thresholds unpinned; earlyoom.earlier_invocation_send_lines, because the contract does not decide its value for a boot with no earlier invocation.",

The journal holds `Suppressed 17 messages from earlyoom.service` at 73499999, one microsecond before ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic=73500000, and the version line `earlyoom 1.9.0` at 73500000 (main.c:161 at earlyoom v1.9.0). Scope is the current invocation's lines in the current boot whose __MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP is >= ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic (round-26/contract.md:78-79), so the suppressed line at 73499999 is outside the scope; rule A2-01 (round-27/contract.md:49; round-26/contract.md:158-159) fires only on a suppressed line in scope, so the version line of the current invocation, which is inside the scope, leaves scope_complete true (round-26/contract.md:92-93). Every other field pinned here is the same pairing that frozen case c19 pins for a version-line-only journal: version 1.9.0 and the verified 1.9.0 grammar (round-26/contract.md:82 and :91), thresholds null and the dry-run flag unset because no threshold line and no `dryrun mode enabled` line is in scope (round-26/contract.md:89 and :92). With no action line in scope and oomd_notices 0 there is no positive evidence (round-26/contract.md:97-98) and nothing forces the unknown verdict (round-26/contract.md:99-101), so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 (round-26/contract.md:102-104). oomd.state inactive and oomd.notices_this_boot 0 follow the oomd show text and the oomd_notices input (round-26/contract.md:95; frozen cases.json c19). Deliberately not pinned: earlyoom.actions, because round-26/contract.md:102 reserves actions null for an inactive or absent killer and frozen case c19 also leaves the counts of an action-free journal unpinned; earlyoom.earlier_invocation_send_lines, because the contract does not decide its value for a boot with no earlier invocation, and a suppressed line is neither a send line nor an escalation line (round-26/contract.md:176).",

line: b380483e2a1d8edc97556fdd021794f619b6e1a6:corpus/knowledge/storage-health-r26.md:132:- SH2 universals (RevRowSH2): "clears them only on an explicit reset" is withdrawn as a universal; removing a device deletes its stored counter item (S132 lines 2294-2324, called from `btrfs_rm_device`), which this one-device host cannot do to its only writable device (S132 lines 2372-2374). The error-level print is rate limited per call site, so counted errors beyond the limit print nothing; error-level lines date some errors, not every error. The capture's grep `BTRFS (error|critical|warning)` cannot match the critical-level `BTRFS: error (device ...)` text; a wave-2 read-only re-run on 2026-10-22 (`journalctl _TRANSPORT=kernel -p warning --grep BTRFS`, all retained boots) found no entries. To select error-level lines use `-p err` or match `BTRFS error (device`.
